hypotheses.justification: `Tr_fixed` takes this instance only because it is instance-implicit and `G` is an argument. The statement does not need it to elaborate. `Tr σ c` is defined as `∑ h, σ h c`, which needs only `[Fintype G]`. Lean drops unused section variables from definitions (`removeUnusedVars` / `Meta.removeUnused` in `Lean/Elab/MutualDef.lean`), so the constant `Tr` does not take `[DecidableEq G]`. The proof does not use it either. It runs `simp only [Tr, map_sum, ← σ_mul_apply]` and then `Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.mulLeft g) _ _ (fun _ => rfl)`, which reindexes a `Fintype` sum by the bijection `h ↦ g * h`. Neither step needs decidable equality on `G`. The result holds for any finite group: `σ g (∑ h, σ h c) = ∑ h, σ (g*h) c = ∑ h, σ h c`. Adding `omit [DecidableEq G] in` before the theorem leaves the statement and proof unchanged.
